notes: The manuscript takes an MD-graph quotient by an edge set C and writes underlined G-prime = underlined G/C as (96), followed by a point. The number is transcribed as written. The editorial statement in H about a prior use of (96) was not treated as source ink or independently checked against another page.

The manuscript presents a canonical diagram, defines Gamma! using automorphisms preserving C and inducing the identity on the quotient, and claims a factorization through the displayed immersion (98). This is a source assertion; no proof of the factorization or immersion property was performed.

The second margin explicitly questions whether these are only local immersions and asks for verification. The third recommends taking the germ defined by a local immersion and then making the group act on it. These are the author’s reservations and proposed reformulation; the reader has not resolved them.

The main text names hatted and unhatted germs from inclusions (98) and (99). The group indices in (99) are both bare, while adjacent M indices remain underlined; in the third margin only the first Gamma index has an underline. These local omissions are preserved without deciding whether they are intended notational distinctions or slips.

The left vertical trace in (97) has a top hook but no lower arrowhead. The canceled right vertical trace has both a hook and a downward head. Direct TikZ within diagram{} preserves these unequal paths and the right cancellation; no completion of the live left arrow is supplied. The upper roofs remain doubtful under the strikes.

The small overworked mark below de before (97) is preserved as a doubtful graphical trace at that location. Its letter content and cancellation state cannot be recovered. The raised group above canceled donc is one continuous une-like word; there is no independently recoverable en. Both witnesses supply en. Although en would make syntactic sense, that consideration is not used to invent its letters or read them into the trace.

The first margin’s déployer is resolved from the single p, tall l and long y-descender. The other indexed doubts, the whole la flèche/l’hom. group and et ce sera, remain open. Verticale, donc and the canceled roofs remain uncertain under crossing strokes. The third-margin target has a bare/hat alternative, bare first, because par’s descender prevents separating an independent roof. Its final formula has no separate terminal period.

Whole diagrams and all formulas with doubts are reproduced as exact TeX in the blind boxes, including the small graphical trace. notes: Physical coverage: 32 reading bands were inspected: 21 primary baselines including the two diagram object rows and caption, the separate (101) label band, nine slanted trial/replacement lines, and pencil foliation 78. The whole scan and both native halves were each viewed once. All 20 saved crops were viewed: 17 initial crops and three documented completion crops for still-open clipped ascenders in filtres/universels and the caption q-descender. The assigned reader did not recrop a decided place during this first reading. No OCR, outside research or TeX compilation was used. This paragraph records only that first-reading workflow; blind-audit records are separate.

The manuscript introduces two starred germs of multiplicities and revises the wording of their construction by traces and removal of divisors at infinity. The long original statement, the shorter taking-traces trial, and non seuls are canceled; their doubtful portions remain explicit. The slanted replacement is read as part of this definition before the live Ils sont donc sentence. The geometry of these germs and the claimed trace/removal construction have not been proved or reconstructed here.

The opening first M has a clear roof and star; the second roof is crossed/overworked and remains doubtful. The M after qui contiennent in the live insertion has an independent roof next to the infini descender, which C omitted. Local index underlines are not uniform: the live multiplicité M_{G-prime} and the two Gamma indices in the canceled final tuple have no separate bars. The inserted M’s small G underline remains uncertain. In (100) both M bodies are bare; a distinction expected from the opening pair does not supply an absent roof. Both raised signs remain star/left-arrow alternatives after the blind audit.

The text calls the germs filtres d’ouverts and describes their fundamental groupoids through a rightward-limit category of categories of revêtements universels, or the subsequent unresolved du connexe wording. Both written ou groups across the line break are retained, the first as doubtful. These are manuscript definitions/assertions; this reading has not constructed the limit, proved equivalence of the descriptions, or used an expected category of coverings to repair the words.
The written cross-reference is comparer [5], n°5, p.768-prime. The right bracket is not a numeral 3. No cited work was identified or consulted, and no external bibliographic claim is made.

Diagram (101) has four objects: the starred two-index M above the lower two-index M; the upper-right M_{G-prime} with a canceled mark; and the lower-left parenthesized M_G with a canceled continuation. Its upper horizontal connection is headless. The vertical arrow points to the lower two-index M, and the lower arrow points right from the parenthesized object to that same target. The author labels the latter équiv d’homotopie !. That homotopy-equivalence assertion and the existence of the germ morphisms are carried as manuscript claims; no proof was performed.

The caption’s abbreviation is équiv with no independent dot. A separate )-shaped stroke above/right of its ordinary closing parenthesis is positioned independently, with attachment uncertain. The ordinary closing stroke descends into the following live des, whose d is retraced; no canceled underlying word is supplied there. The final à/colon mark remains doubtful, and the last phrase ends on this sheet without a completed statement or terminal punctuation.

No ink author page number 39 is visible on this sheet, so none is inferred. The separate pale pencil 78 is kept in margin{}, with its hand unattributed. The asterisk after fondamentaux is transcribed without inventing a footnote or explanation.

Blind audit: all ten differing boxes were personally inspected by root. Four boxes changed: crossed word groups and the live prefix were qualified, both signs in(100) retain star/left-arrow alternatives, and the visible multi-plicités line-end hyphen was restored. The slanted replacement, prose asterisk, universels, two ou groups, abbreviated revêtts/équiv, bracketed reference, diagram geometry and final à/colon doubt were retained. original_record.evidence: The target M has no independently separable two-arm roof. The upper mark meets the descending stroke of par on the previous margin line. Bare M is preferred from the visible contour, while a hat remains possible; the expected ambient object does not settle the stroke. C supplies a hat and H gives a bare M, so neither alternative is declared disproved.

original_record.place: Opening pair: state of the second accent
original_record.evidence: The first M has a simple two-arm roof. Above the second, several angular and transverse strokes cross one another; a clean live roof cannot be separated. The crossed-roof reading is retained as doubtful, independently of the clear star to its right.

original_record.place: Last sentence: reduced mark after lieu
original_record.evidence: The upper component is a small curved cap and the lower component a dark point. This is compatible with the writer’s locally reduced à, but the absence of a full lower letter body leaves a colon alternative. The ambiguity is retained in place.
